summary: Verified INTERACTION_CONTRACT_V1 activation + P1 sub-gaps (4-clock timeouts / idempotent retry replay / stream_state enum). Backend curl-based E2E on the live preview confirms: (a) real /chat/stream turn completes with a populated `interaction` envelope + `request_id` on both meta and done, (b) a follow-up POST carrying `retry_of_request_id=<completed-rid>` short-circuits in 157ms, returns `replayed_from_retry:true` on both `meta` and `done`, identical PONG content, no new LLM invocation (tokens_remaining unchanged), (c) a fresh new prompt with NO retry_of_request_id is correctly NOT replayed (real 2.5s LLM call, different content BANANA), (d) chat/send fallback unchanged, (e) multi-turn context works (session recalled '42'). New unit suites all green: 13/13 timeout_clocks + 10/10 chat_reliability + 6/6 stream_golden_regression. Cross-tenant/tool-failure suites re-verified passing (per main-agent context). UI-level retry-replay could NOT be exercised through the browser because the only available test project (p_demo_a) is disconnected and every UI /chat/stream POST short-circuits with 'connection isn't available' before reaching a real LLM — not caused by this round but blocks live browser proof; backend curl proof is definitive.  The one open question main agent flagged (client-kill mid-stream leaving ledger row stuck at status='started') IS REPRODUCIBLE and STILL OPEN in this preview.

minor.issue: When the HTTP client is killed mid-stream (repro: `timeout 1 curl -N ... /chat/stream`), the chat_request_ledger row is durably written with status='started' BUT never transitions to 'cancelled' even 35+ seconds later. The CancelledError/GeneratorExit except-block at stream.py:820-855 that would call record_cancelled() is not being reached. Matches main agent's own live observation. Likely an ASGI/uvicorn disconnect-signal propagation quirk in this preview environment (worker keeps running past client disconnect); durability guarantee (#4 'task not silently lost') is intact, but positive `cancelled` state resolution is not happening from real network drops. Verified ledger row `5ffde96706174ba5b635bbaaf6bc8499` remained at status='started' 35s after client-kill.

critical_code_review_comments: ChatPanel.jsx's user-facing 'Retry' actions (retryLastFix / retryFailedTurn / regenerate / continueTurn on lines 3207-3246) all route through send(), which resets lastRequestIdRef.current=null on line 3195 BEFORE calling runTurn(). That is INTENTIONAL and correct for user-clicked redo (a genuine new turn should NOT idempotently replay a stale result), but it means the only reachable trigger for a `retry_of_request_id` POST from the real UI is the auto-idle-watchdog performRetry() path (line 2551, fires after 90s of silence) or the inline 'Retry now' button that manualRetryRef binds (line 2653). Worth an explicit docstring noting this design decision so a future reviewer doesn't 'fix' it by wiring user-Retry buttons through the ledger and accidentally re-serving stale content on a manual retry.

The chat/send handler in turn.py accepts retry_of_request_id in ChatBody but does NOT wire it into any ledger check — documented as out-of-scope. Fine for this round; flag for next round if /chat/send ever becomes a live production path again.

rca of the issue: Client-kill mid-stream not transitioning ledger row from 'started' to 'cancelled': the reactive code path (stream.py:820 except CancelledError/GeneratorExit → record_cancelled) is correct and reachable — it depends on uvicorn/starlette signaling a task-level cancel when the TCP peer closes. In this preview environment, uvicorn appears not to abort the running SSE task when the client TCP FINs; the worker continues to completion instead. The ledger design already anticipates this (find_stale_started() reconciler exists in chat_reliability.py) but no scheduled sweeper is calling it, so stale 'started' rows linger. Mitigation options in priority order: (a) periodic background sweep every ~30-60s calling find_stale_started(older_than=hard_deadline_s) and marking them 'unknown' or 'cancelled'; (b) add explicit `await request.is_disconnected()` polls at each yield in the SSE generator; (c) tune uvicorn cancellation propagation (`--timeout-graceful-shutdown` / ASGI lifespan wiring).
